# Teaching with This Book {#sec-966-teaching}

This appendix is for the instructor. It lists what comes with each chapter
beyond the text, and it lays out three fourteen-week course plans that draw on
the same twenty-eight chapters at different depths: an introductory
bachelor's course, a general master's course, and an advanced master's course
that assumes the general one. The chapters were written to be teachable in one
session each, and the plans are built on that unit.

## What Comes with Each Chapter {#sec-966-teaching-materials}

Every numbered chapter carries a banner under its title with four things.

- **The code.** One R script with the chapter's code in the order it runs in
  the book, each chunk under the label the book uses, so that
  `knitr::read_chunk()` can pick a chunk out by name. Chunks the book shows
  but does not run are commented out. The script runs from the folder that
  holds it, beside `_common.R` and the tables the chapters read; a setup
  script installs the packages, pinned where the book pins them
  (@sec-93-package-notes). One archive holds the scripts of all chapters.
- **The exercises as a file.** The chapter's exercises as comments, each
  followed by room to work, after the chapter's data setup so that the
  student starts from the same objects the chapter uses.
- **The solutions.** The worked solutions are @sec-96-solutions, computed at
  render time on the same data; their code is downloadable beside the
  exercises. An instructor who prefers to hand the solutions out later can
  point students at the exercise file alone.
- **Slides**, where a deck exists. The decks are built from the chapter's own
  code and figures, so a figure on a slide is the figure in the book.

The chapter's review status sits in the same banner, and the text can be
annotated in place; @sec-97-colophon-status and the repository's `REVIEWING.md`
say how that works.

## Three Course Plans {#sec-966-teaching-plans}

The plans assume fourteen weeks of one session each, with the chapter read
before the session and the exercises worked after it. They differ in what
they assume and in what they leave out, not in how a chapter is taught.

### An introductory course {#sec-966-teaching-bsc}

For a bachelor's course in portfolio management that follows an introductory
finance course. One chapter a week, the central chapter over two weeks, and
nothing from Parts V, VI or VIII: the course ends where a portfolio has been
built, constrained, tested and costed. The R refresher of @sec-94-r-primer is
read in the first week.

| Week | Chapter | Exercises |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Setting Up Your Environment](01-setting-up.qmd), with @sec-94-r-primer | 1–3 |
| 2 | [Notation and Data](02-notation-and-data.qmd) | 1–3 |
| 3 | [Return, Risk, and the Investor's Problem](03-return-risk-and-the-investor.qmd) | 1–2 |
| 4 | [Descriptive Analysis of Asset Returns](04-descriptive-analysis.qmd) | 1–3 |
| 5 | [Expected Returns](06-expected-returns.qmd) | 1–2 |
| 6 | [The Covariance Matrix](07-covariance-matrix.qmd) | 1–2 |
| 7 | [Mean-Variance Optimization](09-mean-variance.qmd), theory and the two-asset case | 1–2 |
| 8 | [Mean-Variance Optimization](09-mean-variance.qmd), implementation and application | 3–5 |
| 9 | [Portfolio Constraints](12-constraints.qmd) | 1–2 |
| 10 | [Risk-Based Allocation](14-risk-based-allocation.qmd) | 1–2 |
| 11 | [Estimation Error and Its Cost](08-estimation-error.qmd) | 1–2 |
| 12 | [Rebalancing and Transaction Costs](23-rebalancing.qmd) | 1–2 |
| 13 | [Backtesting and Diagnostics](25-backtesting.qmd) | 1–2 |
| 14 | [Benchmarks and Active Risk](24-benchmarks-and-active-risk.qmd), and a review | 1–2 |

: The introductory plan: twelve chapters in fourteen weeks. {#tbl-966-bsc}

Estimation error comes after the optimizer rather than before it, so that the
student has seen what the optimizer does with a sample moment before learning
how little the sample moment is worth; risk-based allocation then reads as
the answer to that problem rather than as a separate topic.

### A general master's course {#sec-966-teaching-msc}

For a master's course in asset allocation that follows a bachelor's course in
investments. Parts I to IV and VII in full, one chapter from Part V, one
sleeve from Part VI, and a week left for the instructor's choice. Two
chapters in a week where one of them is short.

| Week | Chapters | Exercises |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Setting Up Your Environment](01-setting-up.qmd); [Notation and Data](02-notation-and-data.qmd) | 1.1–1.3, 2.1–2.3 |
| 2 | [Return, Risk, and the Investor's Problem](03-return-risk-and-the-investor.qmd); [Descriptive Analysis of Asset Returns](04-descriptive-analysis.qmd) | 3.1–3.4, 4.1–4.3 |
| 3 | [Factor Models and Beta Estimation](05-factor-models.qmd) | 5.1–5.3 |
| 4 | [Expected Returns](06-expected-returns.qmd); [The Covariance Matrix](07-covariance-matrix.qmd) | 6.1–6.4, 7.1–7.4 |
| 5 | [Estimation Error and Its Cost](08-estimation-error.qmd) | 8.1–8.4 |
| 6 | [Mean-Variance Optimization](09-mean-variance.qmd) | 9.1–9.5 |
| 7 | [Risk Measures Beyond Variance](10-risk-measures.qmd); [Higher Moments](11-higher-moments.qmd) | 10.1–10.4, 11.1–11.2 |
| 8 | [Portfolio Constraints](12-constraints.qmd); [Numerical Optimization and Solvers](13-solvers.qmd) | 12.1–12.4, 13.1–13.3 |
| 9 | [Risk-Based Allocation](14-risk-based-allocation.qmd); [Hierarchical and Sleeve-Based Allocation](15-hierarchical-allocation.qmd) | 14.1–14.4, 15.1–15.2 |
| 10 | [Expressing Views](17-expressing-views.qmd) | 17.1–17.4 |
| 11 | [The Equity Sleeve](21-equity-sleeve.qmd) | 21.1–21.4 |
| 12 | [Rebalancing and Transaction Costs](23-rebalancing.qmd) | 23.1–23.4 |
| 13 | [Benchmarks and Active Risk](24-benchmarks-and-active-risk.qmd); [Backtesting and Diagnostics](25-backtesting.qmd) | 24.1–24.4, 25.1–25.4 |
| 14 | The instructor's choice: [Signals and Return Forecasts](16-signals-and-forecasts.qmd) or [Regime-Dependent Allocation](19-regimes.qmd), or a project session | |

: The general master's plan: twenty chapters in fourteen weeks. {#tbl-966-msc}

The chapters left out, 18, 20, 22 and 26 to 28, are the advanced course.

### An advanced master's course {#sec-966-teaching-advanced}

For a second master's course that assumes the general one: Parts V, VI and
VIII in full, the scenario-analysis appendix, and a project. The first week
reopens the three chapters the rest depend on, read again rather than taught
again. Every exercise of a chapter is assigned, because at this level the
exercises are where the chapter is learned.

| Week | Chapters |
|---|---|
| 1 | Reopened: [Estimation Error and Its Cost](08-estimation-error.qmd), [Mean-Variance Optimization](09-mean-variance.qmd), [Numerical Optimization and Solvers](13-solvers.qmd) |
| 2 | [Higher Moments](11-higher-moments.qmd) |
| 3 | [Signals and Return Forecasts](16-signals-and-forecasts.qmd) |
| 4 | [Expressing Views](17-expressing-views.qmd) |
| 5 | [Parametric Portfolio Policies](18-parametric-policies.qmd) |
| 6 | [Regime-Dependent Allocation](19-regimes.qmd) |
| 7 | [Sustainable Investing Constraints](20-sustainability.qmd) |
| 8 | [The Equity Sleeve](21-equity-sleeve.qmd) |
| 9 | [The Fixed Income Sleeve](22-fixed-income-sleeve.qmd) |
| 10 | [The Cost of Forecast Error](26-forecast-error-cost.qmd) |
| 11 | [Decision-Aware Forecasting](27-decision-aware-forecasting.qmd) |
| 12 | [Robustness and Model Uncertainty](28-robustness.qmd) |
| 13 | @sec-965-scenario-analysis: the market with its factors shocked |
| 14 | Project presentations |

: The advanced plan: eleven chapters, one appendix and a project in fourteen weeks. {#tbl-966-advanced}

A project that fits the course is a mandate: a client, a set of constraints,
a policy, and a backtest that reports what the policy cost and where it
failed. The chapters of Part VII are the rubric.
